name: Eudaemonic Bonds

source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Eudaemonic Bonds
Anyone who displays the proper commitment to one of the
cardinal virtues might gain attention from an eudaemon,
but they offer no explanation for why they might single out
some but not others. One person could choose the good
instead of the tempting wrong and feel the eudaemon come
upon them, but another who delivers justice to a villain of
the highest order feels little more than the accomplishment
of a job well done.
Your character, however, stands apart from others of
your kind. Destiny steers your course, or you have a special
talent, or you just have a bit more luck than other folks
have. Provided you meet the requirements listed under the
eudaemons described below, you can apply the benefits
to your character. Note, though, that binding with a
eudaemon comes with some risk. The eudaemons aid those
who embody their virtues, but if their chosen fall short, the
eudaemons deliver swift and terrible punishment.
If you bond with an eudaemon, you will never be alone
again. You feel the entity around you—watching, weighing
your actions, judging you. The eudaemon has no body and
makes no sound, but you know they are always present.
Seeing symbols of the virtue the eudaemon represents
could reflect the actions of the entity, or it might just be
your mind playing tricks, showing you what you expect
to see. If ever you disappoint your eudaemon, you feel
their wrath coursing through your body. Unless you make
amends, you might lose them forever.

2

dog, a woman carrying a serpent and mirror, a compass, or
an open book.

source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Justice
The virtue of Justice requires one to walk between excess
and want and travel along the middle path without ever
straying. Living in balance helps one attain wisdom and
happiness. People touched by Justice also feel compelled to
right obvious wrongs, ensure that those in need receive the
aid they require, and take from those who exploit or harm
others through their greed, selfishness, and wickedness.
Common symbols of Justice include the scales and the
flame of truth.
